gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the three "4K front" two-channel kits write very different amounts of data to the same IMX678 4K 30 fps front picture: 57 Mbps on the Viofo A229 Pro (4K + 2K), 36 Mbps on the Viofo A229 Ultra (4K + 4K) and 32 Mbps in H.265 on the Vantrue S1 Pro Max (4K + 4K), which works out to about 6.9, 8.0 and 10.2 hours of front-plus-rear video on a 256 GB card.
standout_why: Compared against thecargearguide.com (A229 Plus vs Pro vs A329S, and its front-and-rear roundup) and productbible.com (Viofo models compared, and its front-and-rear roundup); caranddriver.com and vortexradar.com refused the fetch, so they were not read. thecargearguide already has measured bitrates and GB per hour for the A229 Plus, A229 Pro and A329S (29/24, 57/25, 65/27 Mbps; about 24, 37 and 41 GB per hour), so the A229 Pro figure itself is not new. Neither site gives any bitrate for the A229 Ultra or the Vantrue S1 Pro Max, neither names the codec, and productbible lists both the A229 Pro and A229 Ultra front as "4K, 30fps, IMX678" as if they were equal. Neither says whether its figures hold with both cameras recording.
decides: It confirms the Viofo A229 Pro 2CH as the pick for front-camera evidence: a DashCamTalk tester measured its full 57 Mbps front with the rear camera attached. It reframes the "best for rear detail" slot: on DashCamTalk's figures a 4K rear comes with about 37% less data on the front picture (A229 Ultra 36 Mbps against A229 Pro 57 Mbps, same sensor, resolution, frame rate and H.264). Our Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K does not win overall on this angle; it honestly wins the 4K-rear segment on price and card time, at $239.99 (Vantrue store, read 2026-11-21) against $409.99 for the A229 Ultra 2CH (Viofo store search, 2026-11-26), with about 10 hours on 256 GB and about 40 hours on its 1 TB maximum. Its front stream is 32 Mbps H.265 against the Ultra's 36 Mbps H.264, so the two are not directly comparable megabit for megabit. One caveat could move this: DashCamTalk does not say whether the A229 Ultra figure was taken in 2-channel or 3-channel use.

findings.label: Recorded bitrate and codec, front and rear (DashCamTalk spec table)
findings.value: Front 3840 x 2160 at 30 fps, 57 Mbps average; rear 2560 x 1440 at 30 fps, 25 Mbps average; H.264
findings.note: Page published 2023-12-22. It does not say which channel configuration the bitrates were measured in; the forum finding below covers that. Sensors on the page: IMX678 front, IMX675 rear; max card 512 GB.

findings.label: Front bitrate with the rear camera attached, against with the interior camera (measured by DashCamTalk member Panzer Platform)
findings.value: 1-channel: 430 MB per 1-minute clip, about 57 Mbps. Front + rear: front stays about 57 Mbps, rear 174 MB per minute, about 23 Mbps. Front + interior: front drops to about 35 Mbps (260 MB per minute), interior about 15 Mbps. Only H.264 available.
findings.source_title: A229 Pro Test & Review PP (DashCamTalk forum, posts #43 and #47, Sep 28, 2023)
findings.note: Panzer Platform (Chuck McCoy) converts file size to Mbps by dividing MB per minute by 7.5 (MB x 8 / 60). He attributes the full front bitrate in front + rear use to an extra processor in the rear camera. Measured on 2023 firmware; later firmware not checked.

findings.label: Recorded bitrate and codec, front and rear (DashCamTalk spec table)
findings.value: Front 3840 x 2160 at 30 fps, 36 Mbps; rear 3840 x 2160 at 30 fps, 35 Mbps; H.264; IMX678 front and rear; max card 512 GB
findings.note: The page labels the figure "Bitrate", not average, and lists an interior camera too (1080p, 35 Mbps), so it is not clear whether 36 Mbps is the 2-channel or the 3-channel figure. Release date given as Aug 2025. Against the A229 Pro's 57 Mbps front: (57 - 36) / 57 = 37% less.

findings.label: Recorded bitrate and codec, front and rear (DashCamTalk review)
findings.value: Front 3840 x 2160 at 30 fps, 32 Mbps average; rear 3840 x 2160 at 30 fps, 24 Mbps average; H.265; IMX678 front and rear; max card 1 TB
findings.note: Published 2026-01-12. Matches the 31.9 / 23.8 Mb/s forum measurement already in Dealectric's record. The same page says the 70mai T800 "comes with a cabin camera making it a much better buy". It does not cover the 4K + 2.5K variant.

findings.label: Normalised: hours of front + rear video per card, from the DashCamTalk bitrates above
findings.value: A229 Pro 2CH: 82 Mbps total, 36.9 GB per hour, 6.9 h on 256 GB, 13.9 h on its 512 GB maximum. A229 Ultra 2CH: 71 Mbps, 32.0 GB per hour, 8.0 h on 256 GB, 16.0 h on 512 GB. Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K + 4K: 56 Mbps, 25.2 GB per hour, 10.2 h on 256 GB, 39.7 h on its 1 TB maximum.
findings.source_title: Vantrue S1 Pro Max (DashCamTalk); with the A229 Pro and A229 Ultra pages cited above
findings.note: Dealectric arithmetic: GB per hour = Mbps x 3600 / 8 / 1000; hours = card GB / GB per hour, taking 1 TB as 1,000 GB. Ignores audio, formatting overhead and space reserved for locked clips, so real figures run a little lower. The A229 Ultra caveat above carries over.

findings.label: Normalised: bits per pixel on the 4K 30 fps front stream
findings.value: A229 Pro 0.23 bit per pixel (H.264); A229 Ultra 0.14 (H.264); Vantrue S1 Pro Max 0.13 (H.265). Rear: A229 Pro 2K 0.23; A229 Ultra 4K 0.14; S1 Pro Max 4K 0.10 (H.265).
findings.source_title: VIOFO A229 Ultra (DashCamTalk); with the A229 Pro and S1 Pro Max pages cited above
findings.note: Dealectric arithmetic: bitrate / (width x height x fps). 3840 x 2160 x 30 = 248.8 million pixels per second; 2560 x 1440 x 30 = 110.6 million. H.264 and H.265 figures are not directly comparable, and I did not source a conversion factor, so the Vantrue figure is shown with its codec rather than adjusted.

findings.label: Maker's recording-time claim against the measured bitrate, both as reported by rival pages
findings.value: productbible: "VIOFO rates 512GB at about six days of 3-hour drives with both cameras", which is 18 h, or 28.4 GB per hour, or about 63 Mbps total. thecargearguide: 65 Mbps front + 27 Mbps rear, about 41 GB per hour, which is about 12.4 h on 512 GB.
findings.source_title: Best Front and Rear Dash Cams (2026): 2-Channel Picks (Product Bible)
findings.note: Second-hand on both sides: I did not open Viofo's own page for the six-day claim (viofo.com returned HTTP 429) or DashCamTalk's A329S review for the 65/27 figures; the second figure is from https://thecargearguide.com/viofo-a229-plus-vs-a229-pro-vs-a329s/ read the same day. The gap of about 30% suggests Viofo's claim assumes a lower bitrate setting. Treat as a lead.

findings.label: What the rival pages already state (so not new)
findings.value: thecargearguide: A229 Plus 29/24 Mbps, A229 Pro 57/25 Mbps, A329S 65/27 Mbps front/rear, about 24, 37 and 41 GB per hour; A329S front 4K 60 fps drops to 30 fps with HDR, and to 4K 30 fps in the 3-channel kit; A229 Plus front 60 fps with HDR off, 30 fps with HDR on.
findings.source_title: VIOFO A229 Plus vs A229 Pro vs A329S: Which to Buy? (The Car Gear Guide)
findings.note: The page credits its bitrates to DashCamTalk's 3-channel reviews. It has no A229 Ultra or Vantrue figures and no codec.
